- title: "Neuro /uniFB01 nd: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders"
- doi: "10.1038/s41398-025-03290-x"
- study_objective: "To present Neuro /uniFB01 nd, a new freely available tool that bridges the gap between the technical expertise and resources required to develop normative models and their accessibility to most researchers. The tool takes structural MRI images as input and outputs two main metrics derived from independent normative models: (1) Outlier Index Score, a deviation score from the normative brain morphology, and (2) Brain Age, the predicted age based on an individual’s brain morphometry."

- association_analysis: "Differences in overall and ROI-level OIS and BAG between patients and respective controls were investigated using an independent-sample t-test or Mann-Whitney U Test. The association between OIS and BAG with symptom severity was tested with Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r) or Spearman’s rho (ρ)."
- key_findings_brief: "The study presents Neuro/uniFB01nd, a web-based tool for normative modeling of brain imaging data, and demonstrates its application in Alzheimer's disease and schizophrenia, revealing distinct patterns of brain deviation and accelerated brain aging."
- key_findings_detailed: "In Alzheimer's disease, 55.2% of patients had very extreme Outlier Index Scores, driven by deviations in temporal-limbic structures and ventricles, and showed homogeneity in their deviation patterns. In contrast, only 30.1% of schizophrenia patients were extreme outliers, with deviations in the hippocampus and pallidum, and they were more heterogeneous than controls. Both groups exhibited signs of accelerated brain ageing."
- key_limitations: "The tool is not customizable for advanced users. It was not developed to identify specific disorders or predict clinical outcomes in a real-world clinical setting. The brain age model has an 'age bias'. The harmonization method may not work for images with unusual quality metrics. The tool may not be suitable for subjects outside the training range (ages 20-80, non-white ethnicities, or MRI scans with field strengths other than 1.5T or 3T)."
- application_notes: "The tool provides two complementary normative metrics: Outlier Index Score and Brain Age. Both metrics are transdiagnostic and derived from whole-brain data, allowing the tool to be applied to a group of individuals of interest without making any assumptions about their diagnoses."
